en: The Sūtra on Entering the Essential Nature of the Dharma Realm,
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta of India during the Sui Dynasty.
At that time, the Bhagavat was staying on Vulture Peak Mountain in the city of Rājagṛha, together with a great assembly.
The Buddha was with a retinue of five hundred people.
At that time, during the first watch of the night, the youth Mañjuśrī came to where the Buddha was; having arrived, he stood at a separate gate of the Buddha’s dwelling.
At that time, the Tathāgata dwelt in samādhi.
Then, the World-Honored One arose from samādhi and saw the youth Mañjuśrī standing outside a side gate; having seen him, he addressed him, saying: "Mañjuśrī!"
"Come, come! Enter within; do not remain outside.
When the youth Mañjuśrī heard the Buddha’s instruction, he addressed the Buddha, saying, "Excellent!"
“World-Honored One,” he said,
and immediately proceeded to where the Buddha was.
Having arrived, he prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and withdrew to stand to one side.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the youth Mañjuśrī:
“You may take a seat.
Then the youth Mañjuśrī said:
“Excellent! World-Honored One, we shall indeed receive your instruction.
Having spoken thus, he joined his palms toward the Buddha and withdrew to sit to one side.
At that time, the youth Mañjuśrī addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One,
by what samādhi does the World-Honored One abide now, from which he has arisen?"
The Buddha told Mañjuśrī:
"There is a samādhi called Ratnakūṭa; at that time, I practiced this samādhi and arose from it."
Mañjuśrī again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“By what causes and conditions is this samādhi named ‘Jewel Accumulation’?
The Buddha told Mañjuśrī:
"It is like a great maṇi jewel that, having been well polished and set in a pure place, produces an inexhaustible supply of various precious gems according to that location."
Thus it is, Mañjuśrī!

Abiding in this samādhi, I observe the eastern direction and see the present Buddhas, Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas in immeasurable asaṃkhyeya worlds. Likewise in the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and above and below—in all ten directions, I clearly behold immeasurable asaṃkhyeya worlds where these Tathāgatas abide in this samādhi, preaching the Dharma for the sake of the assembly.
Mañjuśrī! Abiding in this samādhi, I do not see a single dharma that is not the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu). Mañjuśrī!
Furthermore, this samādhi is named the Seal of the Reality Limit (bhūtakoṭimudrā).
If there are upright men or women who practice this seal, their eloquence will be uninterrupted. Mañjuśrī said:
“Bhagavān, I possess eloquence; Sugata,
I know eloquence.”
The Buddha said,
“Mañjuśrī! How do you understand eloquence?”
Mañjuśrī said: "World-Honored One!
It is as if that maṇi jewel does not rely on any other place, but dwells instead relying upon the very limit of jewels."
"So it is, World-Honored One!
All dharmas have no further place of abiding; they abide solely by relying upon the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*).
The Buddha again addressed Mañjuśrī:
"Do you know the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi)?
Mañjuśrī replied, "So it is,
World-Honored One!"
“I know the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi).
The Buddha said, “Mañjuśrī!
"What is meant by the 'limit of reality' (bhūtakoṭi)? Mañjuśrī replied,
"World-Honored One!"
The limit of "mine" is itself the reality-limit; the limit of all ordinary beings is itself the reality-limit;
whether karma or its retribution, all phenomena are entirely the reality-limit.
World-Honored One!
If one has faith in this way, it is true faith.
World-Honored One!
If one’s inverted faith is itself right faith,
and if one’s non-practice is itself right practice— why is this so?
"Correct and incorrect are merely verbal designations; they cannot be apprehended.
The Buddha said, "Mañjuśrī!"
"What is the meaning of 'practitioner'? Mañjuśrī said,
"World-Honored One!"
"The practitioner is one who perceives the meaning of the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi). The Buddha said, "Mañjuśrī!"
"What is the meaning of 'cultivating the path'? Mañjuśrī replied,
"World-Honored One!"
"The practitioner of the path contemplates the meaning of realization.
The Buddha said, "Mañjuśrī!..."
"How do you teach the Dharma to men and women who are beginners?
Mañjuśrī replied,
"World-Honored One!"
"World-Honored One, regarding those sons and daughters of good family, I teach them to give rise to the view of self; this is precisely how I preach the Dharma for them.
World-Honored One, I do not preach the Dharma by extinguishing the afflictions of desire."
Why is this? Because these phenomena are, by their very nature, neither born nor extinguished.
World-Honored One!
If one can extinguish the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), one can thereby extinguish the limits produced by the view of self (*ātmadṛṣṭi*).
World-Honored One!

For the sake of beginner sons and daughters of good family, I teach the Dharma in this way: they do not accept the Buddha-dharma, they do not cling to the dharmas of ordinary persons, and regarding all dharmas, they neither grasp nor reject them.
“World-Honored One!
For men and women who have first resolved their minds toward enlightenment, I shall preach the Dharma in this manner. Mañjuśrī said:
“World-Honored One, when you also teach and transform sentient beings,
how do you preach the Dharma? The Buddha said, “Mañjuśrī!
I teach the Dharma because form is neither destroyed nor unarisen;
likewise, I teach the Dharma because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are also neither destroyed nor unarisen.
Mañjuśrī! I do not destroy desire, hatred, delusion, and the like when I teach the Dharma. Mañjuśrī!
For the sake of those who teach and transform others, I shall cause them to know the inconceivable Dharma;
it is for this reason that I have attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Mañjuśrī! I have not destroyed any phenomena; having already attained unsurpassed bodhi, there is likewise no arising, yet I have attained unsurpassed bodhi.
Mañjuśrī! That which is called "Buddha" is the dharmadhātu; those various powers and fearlessnesses are also the dharmadhātu. Mañjuśrī!
I do not perceive any divisions within the dharma-realm.
Within the dharma-realm, I do not see that "this is the dharma of ordinary beings," "this is the dharma of arhats," "this is the dharma of pratyekabuddhas," or "these are the dharmas of the Buddhas."
That dharmadhātu is without distinction or superiority, nor is it subject to disruption or confusion.
Mañjuśrī, it is like the Ganges, the Yamunā, or the Kṛṣṇāvatī— when such great rivers enter the great ocean, their waters cannot be distinguished as different.
In this way, Mañjuśrī!
These various names and phenomena enter into the dharmadhātu, where there are no distinctions of name. Mañjuśrī!

For example, just as one cannot speak of distinctions within a heap of various grains, so too within this dharma-realm there are no distinct names—such as "this" or "that," "defiled" or "pure," or "ordinary person," "sage," and "the Buddha-dharmas"—for such names cannot be manifested.
Such is the dharma-realm as I now describe it; such is the dharma-realm that is free from contradiction, and thus should one have faith and delight in it.
Why is this? Mañjuśrī!

Because the realms of the contrary and the compliant and the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu) are non-dual in character, they neither come nor go; because they cannot be seen, they have no place of origination.
After the Buddha had spoken this Dharma, Mañjuśrī again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
"I also do not see the dharma-realm proceeding toward the evil realms, nor do I see it proceeding toward the heavenly or human realms, nor does it proceed toward nirvāṇa.
The Buddha again addressed Mañjuśrī:
"If someone were to come and ask you:
"If one were to ask, 'How is it that there are beings in the six realms of existence in the present?
how would you answer? Mañjuśrī replied:
“World-Honored One!
Regarding such a question, I shall provide an explanation.
World-Honored One!”

For example, suppose there is a person who, while asleep and dreaming, sees either the realm of hell-beings, or the realm of animals, or the attendants of Yama, or the bodies of asuras, or the celestial realms, or human beings and so forth.
World-Honored One!
The dream-visions perceived by those people differ according to each respective path.
Furthermore, when others question them, they speak according to their own inclinations; yet, in reality, those sentient beings do not exist.
"So it is, World-Honored One!
Although I speak of the various paths as being distinct, their dharma-realm is in reality without differentiation,
World-Honored One."
"As for those questioners, I shall explain the matter to them according to reality, because neither [self nor phenomena] exist.
World-Honored One!
If one who practices the vehicle of the śrāvakas seeks to attain nirvāṇa, it is impossible to explain the true meaning to them."
World-Honored One!
Even now, they cannot be distinguished; one can only speak of their names. Why is this?
"Because it grasps the limits of the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*).
World-Honored One!

It is, for example, like the great ocean which possesses seven kinds of jewels—such as *śaṅkha*, jade, coral, gold, silver, *jātarūpa*, and so forth—which can be distinguished from one another by their characteristics."
Within the dharma-realm, its distinct characteristics cannot be known. Why is this?
World-Honored One!

The dharma-realm is neither born nor extinguished; that dharma-realm is neither defiled nor pure; that dharma-realm is neither turbid nor disordered; within that dharma-realm there is nothing that can be extinguished, nor is there anything that is born.
At that time, the World-Honored One, knowing yet intentionally questioning Mañjuśrī, said:
"Do you know the dharma-realm? [Mañjuśrī replied:
"It is so, World-Honored One."
"I know that the dharma-realm is itself my realm.
The Buddha again asked Mañjuśrī:
"Do you know the world?"
Mañjuśrī said: “World-Honored One!
That which is the sphere of action of a person created by illusion is the sphere of the world.”
World-Honored One!
The "world" exists only as a name; no substantial entity can be perceived, yet it is designated as "worldly activity.
World-Honored One!
Nevertheless, I do not perceive the world apart from the dharma-realm.
Why is this? Because there is no such thing as a "world."
As the Blessed One asked:
"Where does the world move?

It is said that the nature of form is neither born nor extinguished; its movement is likewise neither born nor extinguished. Thus it is with feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness: the nature of this consciousness is neither born nor extinguished, and thus its movement is also without birth and without extinction."
“World-Honored One!
Such a single characteristic is, in fact, the so-called ‘characteristicless.
The Buddha asked again:
“Mañjuśrī! Do you not have this thought:
‘If a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha of the present were to enter parinirvāṇa’?”
Mañjuśrī replied:
“World-Honored One,
could it be that within the dharma-realm there is that which has been cultivated and accumulated, or that which has not been cultivated and accumulated?”
“Since the dharma-realm has no cultivation or accumulation, how could there be cessation or non-manifestation?
The Buddha said, “Mañjuśrī!
"What do you think?
Do you not believe that the Buddhas of the past, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, have already entered parinirvāṇa?
Mañjuśrī replied:
“World-Honored One!
I believe that all Tathāgatas have already entered parinirvāṇa, because I see the place from which they emerged.
The Buddha said:
“Mañjuśrī, what do you think?
Do you wish for ordinary beings to be born again after they have died?”
Mañjuśrī said: “World-Honored One!
I do not even perceive the existence of an ordinary person; how, then, could there be rebirth?”
The Buddha asked Mañjuśrī,
“Do you delight in hearing the Dharma in the presence of the Buddha? Mañjuśrī replied:
“World-Honored One!
I also do not perceive the marks of pleasure or non-pleasure.
The Buddha said:
“Mañjuśrī! Do you not delight in the dharma-realm? Mañjuśrī replied:
“World-Honored One!
I do not see a single dharma that is not the Dharma-realm; what else could there be to delight in?
The Buddha said:
“Mañjuśrī! If those who are arrogant hear what you say, they will give rise to great terror. Mañjuśrī replied:
“World-Honored One!

If one who is conceited gives rise to fear, then the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi) also gives rise to terror. Because that reality-limit is not terrified, all dharmas are likewise without terror; because there is no cultivation or fabrication, this is a vajra-word.”
The Buddha said:
“Mañjuśrī, for what reason is this called a ‘vajra-word’?”
Mañjuśrī said: “World-Honored One!
The nature of all phenomena is indestructible; for this reason, it is called the ‘vajra phrase.’”
“World-Honored One!
The inconceivable phrase of the Tathāgata is the inconceivability of all dharmas; it is the vajra-phrase.
The Buddha said:
“Mañjuśrī! For what reason is this further called the ‘Vajra Phrase’? Mañjuśrī replied:
“World-Honored One!
Because all dharmas are without thought, this is a vajra phrase.
World-Honored One!”
"All dharmas are bodhi; this is a vajra phrase.
The Buddha said, "Mañjuśrī!"
"For what reason, World-Honored One, is this further called a 'vajra phrase'? Mañjuśrī replied:
"World-Honored One!"
All phenomena are non-existent; they exist only as names and verbal designations. Of all phenomena, there is neither "this" nor "that," for all are without existence.
That which is without "this" or "that" is suchness (*tathatā*); that which is suchness is reality.
"If it were real, it would be bodhi;
therefore, it is called a 'vajra-word. Mañjuśrī said:
“World-Honored One!
All dharmas are the realm of the Tathāgata; they are adamantine phrases.
The Buddha said:
“Mañjuśrī! For what reason is this called a ‘vajra-word’? Mañjuśrī replied:
“World-Honored One!
Because the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is originally quiescent, this is a vajra phrase.
The Buddha told Mañjuśrī:
"You should summon the bhikṣu Ānanda and have him receive and uphold these words of this Dharma-text. Mañjuśrī said,
"World-Honored One!"
Within this, I do not see a single dharma that can be spoken or heard.
World-Honored One!
I truly do not see even a single syllable that has a locus for being spoken; how could there be many phrases to be upheld?
The Buddha said:
“Excellent, excellent, Mañjuśrī!”
"You have spoken these words well,
Mañjuśrī! I see that in immeasurable asaṃkhyeya worlds in the eastern direction, the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas there also teach this very Dharma-fundamental."
At that time, the Elder Śāriputra emerged from his own dwelling and went to the residence of the youth Mañjuśrī. Upon arrival, not seeing Mañjuśrī there, he proceeded to where the Buddha was.
Having arrived, he stood outside a separate gate of the Buddha's residence.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the youth Mañjuśrī, saying: "Mañjuśrī!
"This bhikṣu Śāriputra is now outside the gate, desiring to hear the Dharma; please allow him to enter.
Mañjuśrī said, "World-Honored One!..."
"Whether it be the limit of Śāriputra or the limit of the Dharma-realm, World-Honored One!
Could these two limits possibly exist internally, externally, or in between the two?"
The Buddha said, “No. Mañjuśrī said:
“World-Honored One!
That which is called the ‘limit of reality’ (bhūtakoṭi) is also not the limit of reality; such a limit and non-limit has neither interior nor exterior, and neither comes nor goes.”
World-Honored One!
The limit of the Elder Śāriputra is itself the limit of reality; the realm of Śāriputra is itself the dharma-realm.
World-Honored One!
Yet this Dharma-realm has no emerging and no entering, no coming and no going; from where, then, did the Elder Śāriputra come, and where is he to enter?
The Buddha said, "Mañjuśrī!
If I were inside, engaged in conversation with the śrāvakas, and you were outside, not permitted to enter, would the thought of suffering and distress not arise in your mind?"
Mañjuśrī said: “No, World-Honored One.”
For what reason?
World-Honored One!
Whatever Dharma is taught does not depart from the dharma-realm; that which the Tathāgata teaches is the dharma-realm, and the dharma-realm is the Tathāgata.
To speak is the suchness of the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu).

The dharma-realm and the realm of verbal expression are non-dual and without distinction; they are non-existent as separate entities. Both the name and the speaker—these are all not apart from the dharma-realm.
World-Honored One!
For this reason, I am not distressed.
World-Honored One!

"If I were not to come to the place where the World-Honored One preaches the Dharma for kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, I would feel neither joy nor affection, nor would I experience any grief or distress. Why is this?"
"If there were duality, then affliction would arise; since the Dharma-realm is non-dual, there is no affliction.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Elder Śāriputra, saying: "Śāriputra!"
"Will you come and listen to Mañjuśrī’s eloquence?
Śāriputra replied,
"Indeed, I will."
“World-Honored One!
I am very eager to hear this. I am currently outside the room, wishing to listen to what the World-Honored One and the youth Mañjuśrī have to say.
At that time, Mañjuśrī addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Please allow the Elder Śāriputra to enter and listen to the Dharma.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Elder Śāriputra, saying:
“Śāriputra! Come forward and enter. Śāriputra said:
“Excellent,
World-Honored One!
He then immediately went forward into the room, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, and withdrew to sit to one side.
At that time, Mañjuśrī said:
"Venerable Śāriputra!
For what purpose have you come here?"
Śāriputra said:
"Mañjuśrī! I have come here for the sole purpose of hearing the Dharma."

There must be the most excellent meaning of the Dharma here, for since Mañjuśrī and the Blessed One dwell together and each has engaged in discourse, there will surely be something sublime and profound; there must be the most excellent meaning of the Dharma.
Then Mañjuśrī said: "So it is, so it is, Śāriputra!"
"I have preached the profound and most supreme Dharma.
Śāriputra said: "Mañjuśrī!"
"In what sense is this teaching profound and supreme?
Mañjuśrī replied, "Śāriputra!"
This Dharma is difficult to know because there are no vessels for it.
Whatever is spoken therein has no point of origination.

This taught Dharma is not for the sake of origination; it is not for the sake of origination for ordinary beings, nor is it for the sake of origination for the Dharma of Arhats. It is the Dharma of the Tathāgata that gives rise to this teaching of the Dharma, because there is neither that which relies nor that upon which one relies. Thus, this teaching of the Dharma is perfectly equal and without any place of abiding.
"Because it explains all dharmas through ultimate quiescence, and because it has no abode,
it is called supreme. Śāriputra said, "Mañjuśrī!"
"For what reason is it said that an Arhat who has exhausted the outflows is not a vessel for receiving this Dharma?
Mañjuśrī replied, "Venerable Śāriputra!"
An arhat has merely exhausted coarse afflictions such as desire, hatred, and delusion; how, then, could they be a vessel?
Śāriputra, for this reason I have said that although an arhat’s outflows are exhausted, they are not a vessel for this Dharma.
Śāriputra said: “Mañjuśrī!

For this reason, I now seek you out—from one place of wandering to another, from room to room, and from cave to cave; I seek you for the sake of the joy of the Dharma, desiring to hear the eloquence of your teaching.”
“Mañjuśrī! I have listened to the Dharma taught by the World-Honored One and by you, yet I am never satiated.
At that time, Mañjuśrī said:
"Venerable Śāriputra!
Are you not content with listening to the Dharma?
Śāriputra replied:
“Mañjuśrī! I do not tire of listening to the Dharma. Mañjuśrī said:
"Venerable Śāriputra!
Can the dharma-realm be grasped through verbal expression?
Śāriputra replied:
"No," said Mañjuśrī, "Venerable Śāriputra!..."

Since there is no weariness in listening to the Dharma, and the dharma-realm is identical with the realm of the Great Virtuous One—being neither two nor distinct—that dharma-realm does not grasp at the teaching of the Dharma; were it to grasp, one might know contentment. Because it does not grasp, therefore there is no contentment.
Śāriputra said: "Mañjuśrī!
Apart from the Tathāgatas, who else could listen to the Dharma in such a manner?"
Mañjuśrī said: "Venerable Śāriputra!
Is that which you call the dharma of nirvāṇa yourself, Śāriputra?"
Śāriputra said: "Mañjuśrī!
I have faith."
Mañjuśrī said: "In what way do you have faith?
Śāriputra replied:
"Because all dharmas are accomplished by their very nature, I have no nirvāṇa.
Mañjuśrī asked again: "Śāriputra!..."
"Do you believe in the deathless Dharma?
Śāriputra replied, "Mañjuśrī!..."
"I have faith.
Mañjuśrī said, "In what do you have faith?"
Śāriputra said:
"As for the Dharma-realm, it neither dies nor is born; I believe it to be thus.
Mañjuśrī asked again:
“Venerable Śāriputra!
Do you believe in Arhats who are devoid of wisdom yet fully possessed of the destruction of the outflows?
Śāriputra replied:
"I have faith. Mañjuśrī said, "In what do you have faith?"
Śāriputra said:
"Because non-wisdom and wisdom are equal, one is fully endowed with the state of an Arhat who has exhausted all outflows. Why is this?"

It is not only that wisdom is free from ignorance; ignorance itself is also free from ignorance. When all phenomena are exhausted, there is no further wisdom, because there is no conceptual discrimination. Thus, being free from wisdom is the Arhat whose outflows are exhausted.
Mañjuśrī asked the Venerable Śāriputra:
"Do you believe in the dharma of liberation of the Arhats whose outflows are exhausted?
Śāriputra replied:
“Mañjuśrī, I truly have faith. Mañjuśrī said:
"How do you have faith?
Śāriputra replied, "Those dharmas are detached from all dharmas; yet, I do not grasp at any dharmas—it is in this way that I have faith."
Mañjuśrī asked the Venerable Śāriputra:
"Do you believe that the former Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, having entered parinirvāṇa, do not attain nirvāṇa?"
Śāriputra said, “I believe.
Mañjuśrī asked again:
"How do you believe this?
Śāriputra replied, "Mañjuśrī!..."
“I believe that this inconceivable realm is neither born nor extinguished.
Mañjuśrī asked the Venerable Śāriputra,
“Do you believe that all Buddhas are one Buddha?”
Śāriputra said, "I believe. Mañjuśrī said:
"How do you believe? Śāriputra said, "Mañjuśrī!..."
"The Dharma-realm is beyond conceptual differentiation; I believe it thus.
Mañjuśrī asked the Venerable Śāriputra:
"Do you believe that all Buddha-fields are one and the same Buddha-field?"
Śāriputra said, "I have faith.
Mañjuśrī asked again:
"How do you believe it?
Śāriputra replied, "Mañjuśrī!..."
"These Buddha-fields are as inexhaustible as Suchness; the fields are also inexhaustible, and I believe thus.
Mañjuśrī asked Śāriputra:
"Do you believe that all dharmas are neither to be realized nor extinguished, neither to be contemplated nor to be cultivated?"
Śāriputra said: "Mañjuśrī!
I have faith."
Mañjuśrī said: "In what way do you have faith?
Śāriputra replied:

“Mañjuśrī! The self-nature does not know the self-nature; the fundamental nature does not abandon the fundamental nature; the self-nature is neither realized nor is there any conceptualization. It is without contradiction, neither arising nor ceasing, neither grasping nor abandoning, and it dwells well within that limit—this is how I have faith.”
Mañjuśrī asked: “Śāriputra!
Do you believe that within the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), there is no phenomenon in the conditioned realm (saṃskṛtadhātu) that arises, nor any that ceases, nor any that accumulates?”
Śāriputra said, "I have faith.
Mañjuśrī asked again:
"How do you have faith?
Śāriputra replied, "Mañjuśrī!..."
"I have such faith that the nature of those dharmas cannot be known as arising or ceasing,
nor as accumulating and abiding. Mañjuśrī said,
"Venerable Śāriputra!"
"Do you believe that within the dharma-realm of prajñā there is even the name 'arhat'?
Śāriputra replied,
"I do believe it."
Mañjuśrī said, "How do you believe? Śāriputra replied:
“Mañjuśrī! To weary of practicing the dharma-realm of prajñā is the realm of the arhat.
However, the essence of the dharma-realm is free from the essences of non-desire, hatred, and delusion; how could an arhat possibly be separate from the dharma-realm?”
"I believe it thus.
Mañjuśrī said, "Venerable Śāriputra!..."
"Do you believe that all dharmas are the realm of the Buddha’s forbearance?
Śāriputra replied,
"I truly have such faith."
Mañjuśrī asked, "How do you have faith?
Śāriputra replied:
“Mañjuśrī! Because the World-Honored One’s fundamental nature is awakening and his self-nature is detached, I believe in him in this way.
At that time, Mañjuśrī said:
“Excellent, excellent, Venerable Śāriputra!
You have explained for me according to your own sphere of experience; since you answered as you did to my questions, I know that there are only this many modes of practice.”
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Elder Śāriputra, saying: “Śāriputra!

If there are sons of good family or daughters of good family who receive and uphold these fundamental phrases of the Dharma, whether they explain them to others, read them, or recite them, those persons will swiftly attain eloquence.”
Śāriputra said: “So it is, Bhagavān! So it is, Sugata!”
"Venerable World-Honored One, as you have said:
World-Honored One!

Yet those sentient beings, having already made offerings to various Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, in previous lives, have been established by those good sons and good daughters in this Dharma-seal; those sentient beings shall attain Great Enlightenment."
At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
What is the name of this Dharma-text?"
"How shall we receive and uphold it?
The Buddha addressed the Elder Śāriputra, saying: "Śāriputra!..."
"This fundamental teaching of mine is titled 'The Buddha’s Explanation as Requested by the Youth Mañjuśrī'; it should be upheld thus.
It is also titled 'Entering the Dharma Realm'; it should be upheld thus.
It is also titled 'The Reality Limit' (*bhūtakoṭi*); it should be upheld thus."

Śāriputra! Those sons and daughters of good family should revere this as a supreme treasure. If they receive, uphold, read, recite, contemplate, or practice according to this Dharma-text, they shall attain the patience of the non-arising of phenomena (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti).

If, for the sake of generating roots of goodness in others, they recite even a little and are then able to extensively explain its meaning to others, they shall attain uninterrupted eloquence (anācchedya-pratibhāna).

When the Buddha had spoken this sutra, Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta and the other bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, the elder Śāriputra and the other bhikṣus, as well as the assembly of devas, gandharvas, humans, asuras, and others, having heard what the Buddha taught, were all greatly filled with joy.
The Scripture on Entering the Essential Nature of the Dharma Realm (Dharmadhātuprakṛtipraveśasūtra)
